note: The fixture pair for blocking-work (L09 in fixtures/PLAN.md), Express and bcryptjs form, scanned with blocking-work alone. Written by hand: each planted defect is fixed in place in the clean twin, line for line, and the twins differ in nothing else. A finding catches a defect when its check matches and its locations name the defect's file, line, column and symbol (every place, when the defect lists several), with the defect's severity. Decoys are in both twins; reporting one is a false positive. The clean twin holds each auto fix as ERLANG writes it, so its lines are long; the guided fix changes the import as well as the call. Paths are relative to each twin. Nothing here is installed or run.

defects.title: PBKDF2 at 600,000 iterations, synchronous, on every signup
bcryptjs's synchronous compare at cost 12 on every login
defects.fixedInClean: crypto.scrypt on the worker pool, checked with timingSafeEqual; bcryptjs is pure JavaScript, so its asynchronous compare would still hash on the request thread

defects.title: The whole export gzipped synchronously
defects.fixedInClean: a worker thread (node:worker_threads) that compresses and returns one buffer; zlib.gzip, awaited, also takes it off the main thread but hands its output back in chunks

defects.title: A file read synchronously on every avatar request
bcryptjs's asynchronous hash at cost 12 on every password change: pure JavaScript, on the request thread in 100 ms slices

decoys.title: randomUUID, which has no asynchronous form and is quick
bcryptjs's asynchronous hash at cost 4 (16 rounds), for a one-time code, through a const
A SHA-256 of the orders' JSON for the export's ETag, made when the orders change: one fast pass, outside any request
A file read once when the module loads
Templates read synchronously at startup, by a function no request calls

bcrypt's synchronous hash in a script no request runs
